correctness.rationale: Double-permutation conjugation reduces a to a rank-two idempotent sandwich. For fixed images u,v,s,t at its two representative points, all other coordinates independently have K(u,v,s,t) choices. An exhaustive 18-type equality/fiber partition table yields the exact seven-base count for every k,l,n. Ratios of its terms establish the fixed-small-block, logarithmic-window, and supercritical asymptotics. Direct enumeration of all ordered pairs at n=2,3,4 and 66 independent parameter table checks pass; finite tests are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new invariant is the total number of pairs commuting under a rank-two full-transformation sandwich. Its seven-base count and logarithmic kernel-size transition are absent from the inspected claims of the closest sources. Tsyaputa classifies kernel types, Dolinka–East treat Green relations/regularity/ranks, and the closest published published-finding corpus text computes a rank-one product fingerprint, not commuting pairs. A historical equivalent remains a residual risk. An existing rank-two variant idempotent commuting-graph claim was compared: its restriction to idempotents does not determine all-element commutation counts.
residual_risks: Unlocated specialized commuting-pair counts of full-transformation variants might be equivalent or stronger.
Tsyaputa classification already makes fiber-size dependence abstractly inevitable, though not the explicit formula and phase transition.
Later or unindexed results could independently contain the seven-base enumeration.

value.rationale: The exact commuting-pair invariant resolves every rank-two full-transformation variant and reveals a mathematically motivated transition in how kernel imbalance changes noncommutativity. A sharp logarithmic crossover with limit (1+exp(-t))^2 separates n^-1 and n^-3 regimes; this is qualitatively more informative than a small finite census or routine substitution of a known rank formula.
